submission.natural_language_explanation: L2/H7 is a retrospective local head (attends mostly 2-3 tokens back) that fires on a token when it and the two or more tokens just before it form one telegraphic run of same-kind items with no article, determiner or verb between them: hex/digit chunks (fused or space-separated, as in hashes, UUIDs, CSS colours, long numbers, phone/IP/version strings), bare number or name lists ("3 7 2 9 4", "John Mary Peter"), juxtaposed category nouns ("red green blue yellow", "cat dog fish"), camelCase pieces, and byte-split non-Latin script (Indic, Thai, Arabic, Hebrew, Greek, Cyrillic), with strength rising from the third item and strongest deep inside long hex/digit or fused-script runs. Ordinary grammatical English prose, the first two items of a run, items separated by 'the'/'a', dense content prose like "Heavy rain caused severe flooding", and runs of single Latin letters stay weak or inactive.

rival_explanations: Word-internal fragment head: it fires only inside runs of non-space-initial subword pieces (fused hashes, numbers, script fragments), so space-separated lists like 'cat dog fish' or '85 cc 30 48' and split camelCase would be inactive.

Function-word-absence head: it fires on any token with no article, determiner or verb in the previous two or three tokens, so content-dense prose without lists, such as 'Heavy rain caused severe flooding yesterday', or noun-compound chains would be active too.
Narrow code/script head: only digit and hex runs and byte-split non-Latin script cross the line, while bare English lists of names, colours or nouns stay inactive.
